blurb: Curly, woolly-coated Spanish all-rounder once used for herding, hunting and fishing
description: The Spanish Water Dog is a medium-sized, athletic Spanish water dog with a curly, woolly coat that can cord, once used for herding, retrieving and fishing work.
answer: The Spanish Water Dog, or Perro de Agua Español, is a medium-sized water dog from Spain. It was traditionally used to herd sheep and cattle, retrieve game in marshlands and help inshore fishermen. Today it is kept mainly as a companion and is known for its curly coat.

body: The Perro de Agua is a traditional Spanish dog population that was always a minority breed. Numbers fell sharply in the 1970s and 1980s as farming and fishing changed, until it was considered at risk of extinction. Researchers identified three sub-populations: the Marismeño of the Guadalquivir marshes, the Serrano of southern Andalucia and the smaller Norteño of Cantabria and Asturias. The FCI definitively accepted the breed in 1999, and in 2012 the Norteño was recognised as a separate breed, the Cantabrian Water Dog.

It is an athletic, robust dog slightly longer than tall, and about half are born with naturally bobbed tails. The curly coat is woolly and may form cords when long. It may be solid black, beige, brown or white, bicolour with white, or particolour; tricolour and tan combinations are not allowed. Males stand 44 to 50 cm and weigh 18 to 22 kg; females 40 to 45 cm and 14 to 18 kg.
The source text gives little detail on temperament. It was a versatile herding, hunting and fishing dog and is now kept principally as a companion.
Sources give little specific detail on care. As an athletic working breed it is generally thought to need regular exercise, and its woolly coat, which can cord, needs owner attention.

Life expectancy is thought to be about 14 years. Conditions reported in the breed through health testing include hip dysplasia, progressive retinal atrophy, hypothyroidism, Addison's disease, exocrine pancreatic insufficiency, allergies, cataracts, distichia, cherry eye and neuroaxonal dystrophy.

faq.q: How big does a Spanish Water Dog get?
faq.a: Males stand 44 to 50 cm and weigh 18 to 22 kg; females are 40 to 45 cm and 14 to 18 kg.

faq.q: How long do Spanish Water Dogs live?
faq.a: Life expectancy is thought to be about 14 years.

faq.q: Does the Spanish Water Dog have a corded coat?
faq.a: Its curly, woolly coat may form cords when it is grown long.

faq.q: Is the Spanish Water Dog recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. It was definitively accepted in 1999 and is FCI breed number 336 in Group 8.
